one_liner: Research AVX2/AVX-512 Round 3 Dilithium code using PSPM-TEE sparse c·s multiplication; paper reports 1.6-2.9x fewer cycles than pq-crystals AVX2.
what_it_does: The repo holds six self-contained source trees (dilithium2/3/5, each as _avx2 and _avx512) of NIST Round 3 CRYSTALS-Dilithium. The README says they are derived from the NIST reference code and PQClean. Each tree exposes NIST-style keypair/sign/verify functions under inconsistent prefixes (XURQ_AVX512_*, dilithium5_sign_avx512, PQCLEAN_DILITHIUMx_AVX2_*), and its Makefile only builds a test_speed cycle-count binary. The numbers it is catalogued for come from arXiv 2306.01989 / IEEE TDSC 2025 ('Optimized Vectorization Implementation of CRYSTALS-Dilithium', Zheng, Zhu, Song, Wang, Zhao). That is the same paper as the Dilithium-AVX512 sibling entry.
how_it_is_fast: PSPM (parallel small polynomial multiplication, from Zheng et al., ACSAC 2022) exploits the fact that the challenge c has only tau coefficients equal to ±1. It packs the small secret polynomials into a precomputed table, so c·s1 and c·s2 become tau shifted adds or subtracts instead of an NTT. PSPM-TEE adds 'tailored early evaluation': it checks the r0 norm before the z norm (r0 rejects more often) one polynomial at a time and aborts at the first failure. The paper credits most of the AVX-512 gain to other work: a 16-way AVX-512 NTT/NTT^-1 with merged layers, 8-way AVX-512 Keccak for matrix and vector sampling, vectorized rejection sampling and packing, and a 'tailored reduction' for q = 2^23 - 2^13 + 1 using AVX-512IFMA.
when_to_use: Studying or porting PSPM-TEE: the repo's PSPMTEE.c shows a 64-coefficient-per-zmm int8-table version of the sparse c·s product with early norm checks
Reading reference AVX-512 kernels for Dilithium (16-way NTT in ntt512.c/inv_ntt512.c, 8-way SHAKE sampling in fips202x8.c and keccak8x.c) when writing your own ML-DSA backend

Checking the paper's component benchmarks: dilithium2_avx512/test/test_speed.c times PQClean ('clean') against the authors' ('xurq') Keccak permutation, matrix expansion, uniform_eta and uniform_gamma1 side by side
Research on Rocket Lake / Ice Lake-class CPUs with full AVX-512 (F/VL/CD/BW/DQ/VBMI/VBMI2), where the paper's i7-11700F numbers apply
when_not_to_use: Any production or FIPS 204 use: the repo is Round 3 Dilithium only (Dilithium2 sk = 2528 bytes) and does not include the ML-DSA code behind the headline Table XI numbers
Anywhere you need a license: there is no LICENSE file, so legally the code is reference-only even though parts derive from permissively licensed PQClean/NIST code

Code you would trust without re-testing. By reading (not running) it: only dilithium5_avx512 signing actually calls pspm_tee_r0/pspm_tee_z, and those functions store |value| (after _mm512_abs_epi32) into z and r0 before z is packed into the signature. The last 64-coefficient block is also loaded at offset N+182-j, versus 192 in pspm()

CPUs without AVX-512 (many client Intel parts, older AMD): the _avx512 trees are compiled with -mavx512f/vl/cd/bw/dq/vbmi/vbmi2, and the AVX2 trees gain only about 3-8% in signing from PSPM-TEE (paper Tables VII/X)
Side-channel-sensitive deployments: the paper says constant-time was 'not the focus', and PSPM-TEE branches on challenge coefficients and returns early from rejection checks

integration.dependencies: none beyond libc; Keccak (XKCP-style KeccakP-1600 times4/times8 files) and Daan Sprenkels' MIT randombytes.c are bundled
integration.min_toolchain: GCC with AVX-512 intrinsics; the paper used gcc 9.4.0, and the dilithium5_avx512 Makefile adds -std=c99
integration.platforms: x86-64 only. The _avx2 trees need AVX2+POPCNT; the _avx512 trees need AVX-512F/VL/CD/BW/DQ/VBMI/VBMI2. Benchmarked only on an Intel i7-11700F (Rocket Lake)
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. dilithium2_avx512/sign.c increments a file-scope 'int count' inside the signing function, so concurrent signing races on it.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it produces Round 3 Dilithium byte formats with NIST crypto_sign-style signatures, but the function prefixes are renamed and inconsistent, the LIB Makefile targets omit the AVX-512/PSPM objects, and it is not FIPS 204 ML-DSA

gotchas: PSPM is not used in most trees: dilithium2_avx512 compiles PSPMTEE.c but signs with NTT, and dilithium3_avx512 plus all three _avx2 trees contain no PSPM code, although the paper describes PSPM-TEE for AVX2 and AVX-512

The test_speed harnesses never check verify's return value (the D5 AVX-512 harness even signs in place over its message buffer). They run NTESTS = 10000, not the paper's 100000 repetitions, so a passing speed run proves nothing about correctness
Build artifacts are committed (common/keccak/*.o and a roughly 20 MB 'our_3_avx512_test_speed' binary in dilithium3_avx512); rebuild from source rather than trusting them
The paper's text and tables disagree on where PSPM-TEE helps most: the text says 7.7% for Dilithium3, while Table VII shows 7.7% for Dilithium2 and 3.1% for Dilithium3
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Dilithium-AVX512 (github.com/Dilithium-AVX512/Dilithium-AVX512) is catalogued from the same paper with the same numbers. It is a single pq-crystals-style tree with KAT files and a DILITHIUM_MODE switch, but it has no PSPM code. Pick this repo only when you want the PSPM-TEE source and the AVX2 variants; for a usable ML-DSA, neither sibling qualifies, and the Plantard-NTT codegen entry is the more rigorous (formally verified) option if you need portable speedups.
verified_claims_summary: On one core of an Intel i7-11700F at 2.5 GHz (Turbo and HT off, Ubuntu 20.04, gcc 9.4.0 -O3 -march=native plus AVX-512 flags, median of 100000 runs), the paper's AVX-512 code needs 36.6-47.4% fewer cycles than the pq-crystals FIPS 204 AVX2 code (e.g. ML-DSA-44 KeyGen 47760 vs 84270 cycles, about 1.6-1.9x). It needs 50.0-65.1% fewer cycles than the Round 3 AVX2 code (about 2.0-2.9x). PSPM alone cuts the Dilithium3 c·s / c·e product by 47-66% versus NTT but only speeds up whole AVX2 signing by about 3-8%. The repo cannot reproduce the ML-DSA table or either full-scheme baseline.
status_note: Stale research dump (10 commits, last 2025-07-16, 3 stars, no issues) with no license, so it is reference-only; treat it as a companion to the TDSC paper, not a library.
